fluff.overview: The Inazuma-class corvette, whose name translates as lightning in Japanese, was the third WarShip design produced by the Draconis Combine in its post-Succession Wars naval rearmament program. Built at the Midway Warship Yard and the Stellar Trek Enterprises Terada Shipyards at Dieron, the class was conceived during the late 3040s as a stealth attack vessel. The Inazuma was intended to approach unsuspecting enemy DropShips and armed JumpShips at high speed, overwhelm them with concentrated firepower, and withdraw before significant opposition could respond. The class embodied an aggressive design philosophy that prioritized speed and offensive capability over crew comfort and defensive protection, reflecting the Combine's emphasis on decisive first strikes in service to the Dragon. Compact and lethal, the Inazuma earned a fearsome reputation among Combine naval officers as the tip of the Admiralty's spear.
fluff.capabilities:
At 200,000 tons, the Inazuma was a compact and fast corvette capable of reaching five thrust points safely with a maximum of eight, enabling acceleration bursts of four gravities. This exceptional speed came at the cost of protective armor, with just 179 tons of improved ferro-aluminum plating providing significantly less coverage than comparable corvettes. A lithium-fusion battery supplemented the Kearny-Fuchida drive, enabling consecutive jumps without recharging and making the vessel exceptionally suited for rapid raids and border interdiction.

The weapons suite was overwhelmingly energy-based, eliminating ammunition dependency for the bulk of its firepower. Four Medium Naval PPCs formed the capital energy battery, concentrated in the nose and broadside arcs, while seven NAC/20 naval autocannons distributed across the quarter arcs, broadsides, and aft provided kinetic capital punch. Anti-fighter defense was formidable, with forty-two ER Large Lasers and twenty PPCs covering all angles of approach, backed by six anti-missile systems for point defense. Three docking collars, six aerospace fighters, and two small craft provided modest escort capacity. Crew quarters were spartanly austere, with only the captain and executive officer receiving full-sized cabins while all other personnel shared bunks in a hot-racking arrangement.
fluff.deployment: The DCS Night of Agony was the lead vessel, stationed outside the Pesht system by late 3058. It was destroyed in November 3072 alongside the DCS Swiping Claw while attempting to break a Word of Blake blockade at Benjamin, with both corvettes and the Kyushu-class frigate DCS Luthien lost in the engagement. The DCS Amber Lotus participated in an attack on the Ghost Bear world of Thule on 29 November 3062, carrying three DropShips into a naval battle against stronger-than-expected resistance. The Amber Lotus survived the Jihad and was redeployed to Midway to defend the Combine's remaining WarShip maintenance facilities but was destroyed on 18 December 3099 at Bikini Atoll during the Second Combine-Dominion War, hunted down by Khan Aletha Kabrinski's Rasalhague task force. The DCS Winds of Heaven was briefly suborned by the Kokuryu-kai during the early Jihad before being recaptured by the Internal Security Force. It survived the Jihad and engaged the Dominion battleship Ursa Major at Rasalhague in 3100, sustaining severe damage but escaping. The Winds of Heaven remained one of only two surviving Combine WarShips into the ilClan era, held in strategic reserve.
fluff.history:
The Inazuma program was part of the Draconis Combine Admiralty's ambitious effort to rebuild a meaningful naval capability in direct response to the devastating Clan Invasion of the early 3050s. The corvette was the third class in the Combine's new WarShip construction initiative, designed to complement heavier cruiser and frigate designs already under construction at Combine shipyards. Construction of the Inazuma class was divided between two facilities: the Midway Warship Yard in the Midway system, which produced the majority of the hulls, and the Stellar Trek Enterprises Terada Shipyards at Dieron, which had been rebuilt for WarShip production in 3055. The Combine invested heavily in both yards, viewing the corvette program as essential to establishing a credible naval screening force. All four completed vessels were spaceworthy by 3058 and quickly dispersed across the Combine's naval commands.

A fifth hull under construction at the Terada Shipyards was destroyed by unknown saboteurs in 3065, dealing a significant blow to the program. Although the shipyard was rebuilt by 3066, the Admiralty cancelled plans for further corvette construction, choosing instead to focus the facility on supporting existing vessels. This decision effectively capped the class at four hulls, making every vessel irreplaceable.

The Jihad proved devastating for the small fleet. Two corvettes were lost during Combine naval operations against the Word of Blake in 3072. The losses were compounded by a Word of Blake raid on the Midway Shipyards in 3074 that ended WarShip production there entirely, eliminating any possibility of replacing the fallen vessels. Only two of the original four corvettes survived into the post-Jihad era, and the Combine Admiralty treated both as strategic assets too valuable to risk in anything short of existential engagements. Continued attrition during the Wars of the Republic Era claimed another hull, leaving a single Inazuma in Combine service. That lone corvette remained one of only two operational Combine WarShips well into the ilClan era, held in strategic reserve as an irreplaceable remnant of the Admiralty's once-ambitious rearmament program.
